claims.text: The proposed intervention consists of adding approximately 1–2 atomic percent Nb during synthesis and applying a controlled single-step thermomechanical treatment.
Nb microalloying combined with the thermomechanical treatment will induce in-situ formation of coherent nanoscale precipitates.
The induced nanoscale precipitates will be uniformly dispersed along colony or phase boundaries.
The nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion through Orowan strengthening.
The nanoscale precipitates will provide sites for effective strain accommodation.
Obstruction of dislocation motion will enhance yield strength.
Effective strain accommodation at the precipitates will enhance ductility.
The treated alloy will have a 20–30% higher yield strength than an alloy without Nb addition and the tailored treatment.
The treated alloy will have a 10–20% higher elongation to failure than an alloy without Nb addition and the tailored treatment.
The predicted improvements should occur under room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The beneficial effects will occur only within a narrow range of Nb concentrations and precisely controlled thermomechanical-processing conditions.
Departures from the proposed composition or processing window may produce undesirable brittle intermetallic phases.
Formation of brittle intermetallic phases may mask or negate the intended strength and ductility improvements.
The baseline alloy lacks Nb microalloying and controlled nanoprecipitate formation and consequently has lower yield strength and ductility.
